entries.description: Root cause fixed: Pironman apply path returned frequent 'apply busy: previous apply still running' under repeated UI submits. Implemented helper-side serialized apply queue worker with burst coalescing, and frontend submit lock to prevent concurrent applies. Deployed to Pi and validated service health/runtime logs.

Definitive root cause identified: helper used CLI restart/read path that did not represent live Pironman state reliably under this firmware, causing apparent non-application and stale readback. Remediation switched helper to official Pironman API v1.0 endpoints for granular set/get with queued apply orchestration preserved; verified live on Pi via helper socket apply+read showing consistent persisted values.

Future enhancement: keep manual Apply as default, but add optional debounced auto-apply mode behind a feature flag for users who want faster UX. Also add Pi5 CPU budget guardrails and diagnostics snapshots for ultron-ap/ultron-helper/Pironman stack; current live sample shows Ultron processes low CPU while extra steady CPU comes from pironman5-service and influxd.

Non-intrusive policy hardening: removed helper fallback to pironman CLI read path and changed hardware availability check to require real Pironman runtime reachability. This prevents Ultron from implying hardware availability when Pironman stack is down and avoids host-side side effects from fallback execution.

Phase 2 completed: removed hardware module from Ultron core runtime (`/hardware` route, apply endpoint, handlers, and templates). Updated contract checks to enforce core decoupling while preserving helper-side stability/security controls. Verified with `go test ./...`, generated hardware-stability tests, and `aitri verify --feature hardware-stability-refactor`.

Completed optional-integration hardening: Settings now exposes on-demand integration diagnostics with Pironman capability states (`available|unavailable|degraded`) and process-level CPU/RAM attribution for `ultron-ap`, `ultron-helper`, `pironman5-service`, and `influxd`. Added explicit operations policy forbidding core lifecycle management of Pironman/Influx.
